tier_reason: First-party numbers with public paired harness (bench/run_benchmarks.py, bench/*.wren, bench/lua_equivalents/*.lua, results in bench/results.json) and CPU stated (Apple M4 Pro), but the C compiler is not named and the LuaJIT build flags are not stated, so not A; no independent measurement, so not B.

corrections.baseline: LuaJIT 2.1 with JIT on (docs/index.html report names LuaJIT 2.1.1785763465; build flags not stated); the report also shows a LuaJIT -joff column
corrections.claimed_speedup: README microbenchmark table, WrenJIT vs LuaJIT time (lower is better): sum 0.641 ms vs 1.092 ms (0.59x), range for 0.074 ms vs 0.584 ms (0.13x), fib(35) 39.4 ms vs 51.9 ms (0.76x), tak 2.224 ms vs 6.361 ms (0.35x), ack(3,7) 0.024 ms vs 1.066 ms (0.02x), mutual recursion 0.098 ms vs 0.321 ms (0.31x), deep recursion 0.625 ms vs 6.724 ms (0.09x), binary trees 8.807 ms vs 19.8 ms (0.45x), method call 0.087 ms vs 0.448 ms (0.19x). Five of these rows do not time equivalent work: range for and method call are computed in closed form by optimizer passes 15-16 (irOptFastForwardRangeSum, irOptFastForwardToggleCounter), ack is replaced by the closed form 2^(n+3)-3 for m=3, mutual recursion by a parity test, and deep recursion is collapsed into a loop, while LuaJIT runs the real loops and calls; binary trees run a hand-written C tree builder and walker. Rows with comparable work: sum 0.59x, fib 0.76x, tak 0.35x. The author's own published report (docs/index.html, ten Benchmarks Game ports) says WrenJIT is faster than LuaJIT on 1 of 10: pidigits 66.4 ms vs 119.8 ms (0.55x); slower on the rest, e.g. nbody 848.4 ms vs 31.8 ms (26.69x slower), regex-redux 19.06x, k-nucleotide 5.68x, fasta 5.25x, binary-trees 4.25x, fannkuch-redux 3.63x, mandelbrot 3.15x, spectral-norm 1.68x, reverse-complement 1.58x.
corrections.caveats: The README calls these 'narrow kernels, not a language-wide victory lap'. Several microbenchmark rows measure benchmark-shaped special cases rather than JIT code doing the same work as LuaJIT: src/jit/wren_jit_recursion.c recognizes exact bytecode shapes and emits Ackermann as the closed form 2^(n+3)-3 (no recursion), mutual even/odd recursion as a single parity test, linear recursion as a loop, and binary-tree make/check through hand-written C (treeMakeFill and a C tree walker); optimizer passes 15-16 in src/jit/wren_jit_opt.c fast-forward range sums and boolean toggle counters in closed form (the report admits these are 'reduced as recurrences instead of paid one iteration at a time'). Outputs are correct and the specializations are guarded, but the 0.02x-0.19x rows say nothing about general Wren code. On the author's ten paired Benchmarks Game ports (docs/index.html; also bench/benchmarksgame_results.json from an earlier run) WrenJIT is slower than LuaJIT on 9 of 10 programs (up to 26.7x slower on nbody) and slower than the plain Wren interpreter on k-nucleotide; only pidigits wins. Programs are separate Wren and Lua ports, self-timed with System.clock/os.clock, best of five, sub-millisecond timings on several rows; Wren timer includes JIT warmup. C compiler not named; LuaJIT build flags not stated. Single author, 4 stars, repo started 2026-02-22.

notes: Numbers in the record match the README table exactly, but the claim is overstated: ack, range for, method call and mutual recursion are closed-form or O(1) replacements, deep recursion is collapsed to a loop and binary trees run hand-written C, so only sum/fib/tak (0.59x/0.76x/0.35x) compare like work. The author's own published report shows WrenJIT slower than LuaJIT on 9 of 10 Benchmarks Game ports (faster only on pidigits 0.55x). Kept at tier C with these shortcomings (results are correct and disclosed, so not a reject under the invalid-evidence rule); metadata checked: MIT, 4 stars, last commit 2026-08-14, not a fork.

tier_reason: First-party README table; a public cross-runtime harness exists (benchmarks/run.sh with bench_fib.xs/.py/.js/.go, results in benchmarks/results.json) but the CPU model ('AMD Ryzen 7'), compiler and which build (default gcc -O2 or make release -O3 -flto) are not stated, so C.

corrections.baseline: CPython 3.13 and Node 20 (V8), measured in the same README table; the Node column is dominated by Node's own 57 ms process startup
corrections.claimed_speedup: README table (wall time including process startup, best of three): fib(30) XS --jit 31 ms vs Node 20 62 ms vs Python 3.13 71 ms (--vm 180 ms, --interp 950 ms); hello world startup XS 3 ms vs Node 57 ms vs Python 15 ms. Subtracting each runtime's hello-world startup, fib(30) compute is about 28 ms for XS --jit vs about 56 ms for CPython (about 2x faster) and about 5 ms for Node (XS about 5x slower than V8) (derived from page data). The committed cross-runtime run (benchmarks/results.json, 2026-05-03, best of 5) shows fib XS --jit 0.038 s vs python3 0.083 s vs node 0.117 s vs go 0.005 s, and mandelbrot XS --jit 0.577 s vs python3 0.338 s vs node 0.112 s, i.e. XS slower than both CPython and Node on mandelbrot.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Not stated for the README table; Makefile default build is gcc -O2 -std=c11, make release is -O3 -flto -DNDEBUG; which build produced the table is not said
corrections.workload: README: two programs run cold from disk with wall time including process startup: hello world (startup) and recursive fib(30); XS shown in --interp, --vm and --jit modes; best of three runs. The repo's benchmarks/run.sh adds sort, mandelbrot, nbody, json, strings, hash and startup ports in XS, Python, JavaScript and Go.
corrections.caveats: The README says 'treat as indicative, not authoritative'. Only one compute benchmark (call-bound recursive fib) is shown, and every timing includes process startup: Node 20's 57 ms startup is almost all of its 62 ms fib(30) time, so the apparent 2x win over Node is a startup artifact and on compute XS --jit is about 5x slower than V8 (derived from page data); the win over CPython (about 2x on fib compute) is real on this one kernel. The README omits the repo's own mandelbrot result (benchmarks/results.json: XS --jit 0.577 s vs CPython 0.338 s vs Node 0.112 s), where XS is slower than both baselines; the other rows in that file (sort, nbody, json, strings, hash) run 1-30 ms and are dominated by Python and Node startup. The reproduction pointer tests/bench_backends.sh only compares XS's own backends (median, fib(28), no Node or Python); the cross-runtime harness is benchmarks/run.sh. In the 2026-04-24 benchmarks/baseline.json the JIT was no faster than the VM (fib 0.155 s vs 0.150 s). CPU model ('AMD Ryzen 7') and compiler/build not stated. XS is its own language, not a drop-in for JavaScript or Python programs, and is unrelated to the Moddable XS JavaScript engine.

notes: Separate project, not a duplicate: xs-lang0/xs is a new standalone language (own syntax, compiler, VM and JIT, Apache-2.0, 489 commits) with no relation to the Moddable XS JavaScript engine already listed under embedded-scripting. README numbers match the record, but the claim is overstated: the Node comparison is startup-dominated (V8 compute about 5 ms vs XS about 28 ms on fib(30), derived) and the repo's own results.json shows XS slower than CPython and Node on mandelbrot; only the fib win over CPython holds.
